basics.description: **Abstract to Sentinel: app registration created by script** Abstract Security: a security data pipeline and agentic SIEM in one platform. The portal-wizard variant of the Sentinel destination: a deployment script creates the Entra app registration and, with Key Vault, its client secret, then the template builds the same ingestion stack. It runs as a tier-0 managed identity you create beforehand, so it suits portal-only teams and labs. The data plane, plus a deployment script that creates the Abstract app and stores its secret in Key Vault.

location.label: Region
location.toolTip: The Azure region of the workspace, the Data Collection Endpoint and Rule, the Key Vault and the deployment script. The endpoint and rule must sit in the workspace's region. Find it: Azure portal > Resource groups > your group > Overview > Location. Example: eastus. Default: the resource group's region.

options.text: The data plane, plus a deployment script that creates the Abstract app and stores its secret in Key Vault.

basics.name: depth
basics.label: Setup depth
basics.toolTip: Recommended settings shows only what most deployments set and keeps every other setting at its default. Show every setting adds a More settings section to each tab. Hidden settings are sent with their defaults, so either choice deploys.

options.text: Questions or help with this deployment: email support@abstract.security or use the contact page at https://www.abstract.security/contact-us.

body.query: [concat('resources | where subscriptionId =~ "', subscription().subscriptionId, '" and type =~ "microsoft.operationalinsights/workspaces" and resourceGroup =~ "', resourceGroup().name, '" | project name, location, resourceGroup, subscriptionId, id = tolower(id) | join kind=leftouter (resources | where type =~ "microsoft.operationsmanagement/solutions" and name startswith "SecurityInsights(" | project id = tolower(tostring(properties.workspaceResourceId)), hasSentinel = 1) on id | extend sentinel = iff(isnotnull(hasSentinel), "yes", "no") | project name, location, resourceGroup, subscriptionId, id, sentinel | order by name asc')]

elements.name: workspaceMode
elements.label: Create a new workspace
elements.toolTip: On creates a Log Analytics workspace and switches Microsoft Sentinel on. Off uses a workspace that already runs Microsoft Sentinel in this resource group, and nothing about that workspace (pricing tier, retention, daily cap, network) is changed. A new workspace is a new billable resource, and pointing Abstract at a second workspace splits your data. Find it: Azure portal > Microsoft Sentinel, which lists every workspace that runs it with its resource group. Default: on.

elements.name: workspaceNameNew
elements.label: New workspace name
elements.toolTip: The Log Analytics workspace Abstract writes to. For a new workspace, leave it empty to generate abstract-sentinel-<suffix>, or give 4 to 63 letters, digits and hyphens; the name cannot be changed later. For an existing workspace, its exact name: it must be in this resource group, or the deployment fails. Find it: Azure portal > Log Analytics workspaces > Name. Example: sentinel-prod.

validations.message: 4 to 63 letters, digits and hyphens, starting and ending with a letter or digit.
A workspace with this name is already in this resource group. Choose Use existing instead, or pick another name.

elements.name: workspaceExisting
elements.label: Existing Microsoft Sentinel workspace
elements.toolTip: The Log Analytics workspace Abstract writes to. For a new workspace, leave it empty to generate abstract-sentinel-<suffix>, or give 4 to 63 letters, digits and hyphens; the name cannot be changed later. For an existing workspace, its exact name: it must be in this resource group, or the deployment fails. Find it: Azure portal > Log Analytics workspaces > Name. Example: sentinel-prod. The list shows the workspaces in this resource group that run Microsoft Sentinel, read live from Azure Resource Graph.

elements.name: workspaceRetentionDays
elements.label: Retention of a new workspace
elements.toolTip: How many days a new workspace keeps data searchable, 7 to 730. Used only when the deployment creates the workspace; an existing workspace is never changed. The Abstract table's own retention is a separate setting. Find it: Azure portal > Log Analytics workspaces > the workspace > Usage and estimated costs > Data retention. Example: 180. Default: 90.

elements.name: workspaceSku
elements.label: Pricing tier of a new workspace
elements.toolTip: The pricing tier the deployment gives a new workspace. PerGB2018 is the standard pay-as-you-go tier, and the only one offered here, as in the earlier form: the template sets no capacity reservation level. An existing workspace keeps its tier. Find it: Azure portal > Log Analytics workspaces > the workspace > Usage and estimated costs. Example: PerGB2018. Default: Pay-as-you-go (PerGB2018).

elements.name: enableSentinel
elements.label: Switch Microsoft Sentinel on
elements.toolTip: Switches Microsoft Sentinel on for a new workspace. Used only when the deployment creates the workspace; an existing workspace is assumed to run Microsoft Sentinel already. Turned off, the ASIM tables and every Microsoft Sentinel feature are missing from the new workspace. Find it: Azure portal > Microsoft Sentinel > the workspace. Default: on.

body.query: [concat('resources | where subscriptionId =~ "', subscription().subscriptionId, '" and resourceGroup =~ "', resourceGroup().name, '" and type in~ ("microsoft.insights/datacollectionendpoints", "microsoft.insights/datacollectionrules") | project name, location, dcKind = iff(type =~ "microsoft.insights/datacollectionendpoints", "dce", "dcr"), isAbstract = iff(isnotnull(properties.streamDeclarations["Custom-', if(equals(basics('depth'), 'all'), coalesce(steps('ingestion').advanced.customTableName, ''), 'AbstractEventLogs_CL'), '"]), "yes", "no"), flows = coalesce(array_length(properties.dataFlows), 0) | order by name asc')]

options.text: Abstract sends every event to one Data Collection Rule through one Data Collection Endpoint, into the Abstract table. The table has one column per top-level key of the Abstract Common Schema event, which is how the Abstract Azure Sentinel Destination sends it. The log stream name you enter in Abstract is Custom-<table name>.

Use existing to run again over the endpoint an earlier run created: the deployment re-applies this template's settings to it (public network access on, these tags), and other rules that use it keep working. The endpoint must be in the workspace's region. Find it: Azure portal > Monitor > Settings > Data Collection Endpoints. Default: Create new.

elements.name: dcrMode
elements.label: Data Collection Rule
elements.toolTip: Create new for a first install. Use existing only for a rule an earlier run of this template or the solution created: the deployment replaces the rule's stream declarations, destinations and dataflows, and keeps its immutable ID, so Abstract keeps sending without a change. Find it: Azure portal > Monitor > Settings > Data Collection Rules. Default: Create new.

elements.name: dcrNameNew
elements.label: New rule name
elements.toolTip: The name of the new Data Collection Rule. Its immutable ID, a deployment output, is what you enter in Abstract. The form refuses a name already used by a rule in this resource group. Find it: Azure portal > Monitor > Settings > Data Collection Rules. Example: abstract-dcr-prod. Default: abstract-dcr.

validations.message: 3 to 64 letters, digits, periods, underscores and hyphens.

A Data Collection Rule with this name is already in this resource group, and deploying would replace its streams, destinations and dataflows. Choose Use existing to do that on purpose, or pick another name.

Find it: Azure portal > Monitor > Settings > Data Collection Rules. Example: abstract-dcr.

elements.name: customTableName
elements.label: Abstract table name
elements.toolTip: The custom table that receives every Abstract event. It must end in _CL. The log stream name you enter in Abstract is Custom-<this name>, so changing it means changing the destination in Abstract too. Find it: Azure portal > Log Analytics workspaces > the workspace > Tables. Example: AbstractEventLogs_CL. Default: AbstractEventLogs_CL.

validations.message: Letters, digits and underscores, starting with a letter and ending in _CL.

elements.name: tableColumns
elements.label: Table columns (JSON)
elements.toolTip: Leave it empty to use the generated Abstract Common Schema: one column per top-level key of the event Abstract sends, with a rule transformation that sets TimeGenerated. Supply columns only for a custom payload shape; the rule then uses these columns and the transformation below, and the ASIM routes need the generated schema. Example: [{"name": "TimeGenerated", "type": "datetime"}, {"name": "Message", "type": "string"}].

validations.message: A JSON array of columns, or [] for the generated schema.

elements.name: customTablePlan
elements.label: Plan of the Abstract table
elements.toolTip: The table plan of the Abstract table. Keep leaves an existing table's plan alone and creates a new table as Analytics, so a redeploy never changes it by accident. Analytics runs analytics rules and the Abstract content; Basic has limited queries; Auxiliary is the data lake tier, with no analytics rules or alerts. A plan set here applies to the whole table. Find it: Azure portal > Log Analytics workspaces > the workspace > Tables > the Abstract table > Plan. Example: Analytics. Default: Keep (a new table starts on Analytics).

allowedValues.label: Keep (a new table starts on Analytics)

elements.defaultValue: Keep (a new table starts on Analytics)

elements.name: customTableRetentionDays
elements.label: Total retention of the Abstract table
elements.toolTip: Total retention of the Abstract table in days. 0 sends no retention: an existing table keeps its own and a new one takes the workspace's. Shortening it deletes data older than the new value. Find it: Azure portal > Log Analytics workspaces > the workspace > Tables > the Abstract table > Total retention. Example: 365. Default: 0.

elements.name: enableDcrErrorLogs
elements.label: Record ingestion errors in DCRLogErrors
elements.toolTip: Sends the rule's ingestion errors (refused requests, malformed rows, transformation and limit errors) to the DCRLogErrors table. Leave it on: the ingestion API answers before it validates, so without it data Azure drops is invisible to you and to Abstract. Turn it off only if another diagnostic setting already collects these errors. Find it: Azure portal > Log Analytics workspaces > the workspace > Logs > DCRLogErrors. Default: on.

elements.name: tagsByResource
elements.toolTip: Tags for one kind of resource only, keyed by the full Azure resource type, added to the tags every created resource gets. Use it when the workspace, the endpoint and the rule need different tags. Find it: Azure portal > each created resource > Tags. Example: {"Microsoft.Insights/dataCollectionRules": {"owner": "secops"}}.

elements.name: grantMonitoringContributor
elements.label: Also grant Monitoring Contributor on the rule
elements.toolTip: Off by default: sending data needs only Monitoring Metrics Publisher, which is always granted. Monitoring Contributor would let a leaked Abstract credential rewrite or delete the rule and its error-log setting. Turn it on only if your Abstract setup asks for it. Find it: Azure portal > Monitor > Data Collection Rules > the rule > Access control (IAM). Default: off.

options.text: ASIM tables are off by default. When on, every ASIM analytics rule, hunting query and workbook already running in this workspace also reads Abstract data: expect new alerts, duplicate events where Microsoft's own connector collects the same vendor, and a second billed copy of each mapped event. Turn it on in a staging workspace first, or one schema at a time.

elements.name: enableAsim
elements.label: Also write Microsoft's ASIM tables
elements.toolTip: Also writes each event into the Microsoft ASim table for its schema (ASimAuthenticationEventLogs, ASimNetworkSessionLogs and the others), mapped from the Abstract Common Schema, so Microsoft's ASIM analytics rules, hunting queries and workbooks see Abstract data. Expect new alerts, and duplicates where a Microsoft connector already collects the same vendor. Needs Microsoft Sentinel on the workspace. Find it: Azure portal > Log Analytics workspaces > the workspace > Tables, the ASim tables. Default: off.

elements.name: asimSchemas
elements.label: ASIM schemas
elements.toolTip: The ASIM schemas to write when ASIM is on, one ASim table each: AuditEvent, Authentication, Dns, FileEvent, NetworkSession, ProcessEvent, RegistryEvent and WebSession. Narrow the list to bring ASIM in one schema at a time. Each schema is one dataflow of the 20 a rule allows. Find it: Azure portal > Log Analytics workspaces > the workspace > Tables, the ASim tables. Example: ["Authentication", "NetworkSession"]. Default: every schema.

options.text: The user-assigned identity you supply runs the provisioning script; it is separate from Abstract's runtime app. Before the deployment, a Global Administrator must grant it Microsoft Graph Application.ReadWrite.All (AppRoleAssignment.ReadWrite.All is not needed) with admin consent, once per tenant. With no Key Vault, no secret is created; create one in Entra after the deployment and copy its value once.

[concat('The Key Vault this deployment creates and the deployment script go in ', location(), ', the region chosen on Basics. The Data Collection Endpoint and Rule go in the workspace region. An existing Key Vault and the provisioning identity stay where they are, in any region or subscription.')]

elements.name: managedIdentityResourceIdMode
elements.label: How to choose the provisioning identity
elements.toolTip: Pick lists the user-assigned managed identities you can see, in every subscription. Enter the resource ID is for an identity the list does not show, such as one in a subscription you cannot browse. Find it: Azure portal > Managed Identities. Default: Pick from a list.

elements.name: managedIdentityResourceIdPick
elements.label: Provisioning identity
elements.toolTip: The user-assigned managed identity the deployment script runs as. A Global Administrator must have granted it Microsoft Graph Application.ReadWrite.All with admin consent, once per tenant, or the script cannot create the app. The list does not show whether that grant exists. Find it: Azure portal > Managed Identities > the identity > Properties > Id. Example: abstract-deployer.

elements.name: managedIdentityResourceIdBlock
elements.label: Selection required
elements.toolTip: Select the provisioning identity in the list above, or choose Enter the resource ID instead.

validations.message: Select the provisioning identity in the list above, or choose Enter the resource ID instead.

elements.name: managedIdentityResourceIdManual
elements.label: Provisioning identity
elements.toolTip: The full resource ID of the user-assigned managed identity the deployment script runs as to create the Abstract app. It can be in another resource group or subscription. Before the deployment a Global Administrator must grant it Microsoft Graph Application.ReadWrite.All with admin consent, once per tenant, or the script cannot create the app. Find it: Azure portal > Managed Identities > the identity > Properties > Id. Example: /subscriptions/00000000-0000-0000-0000-000000000000/resourceGroups/rg-identity/providers/Microsoft.ManagedIdentity/userAssignedIdentities/abstract-deployer.

validations.message: The full resource ID of a user-assigned managed identity.

elements.name: keyVaultMode
elements.label: Where the client secret is kept
elements.toolTip: Create makes a new Key Vault and stores the client secret in it; Existing stores it in a vault you name; None creates no secret, and you create one in Entra after the deployment and copy its value once. Find it: Azure portal > Key vaults. Example: Create. Default: Create a new Key Vault.

allowedValues.label: No Key Vault: create the secret in Entra afterwards

elements.name: keyVaultName
elements.label: New Key Vault name
elements.toolTip: The name of the new Key Vault, 3 to 24 lowercase letters, digits and hyphens, unique across Azure. Leave it empty to generate abskv-<suffix>. Used only when the deployment creates the vault. Find it: Azure portal > Key vaults. Example: abskv-secops.

validations.message: 3 to 24 lowercase letters, digits and hyphens, starting with a letter, or empty to generate one.

elements.name: existingKeyVaultResourceIdMode
elements.label: How to choose the Key Vault
elements.toolTip: Pick lists the Key Vaults you can see, in every subscription. Enter the resource ID is for a vault the list does not show. The provisioning identity gets Key Vault Secrets Officer on the vault you choose. Find it: Azure portal > Key vaults. Default: Pick from a list.

elements.toolTip: The vault that will hold the client secret. It must use Azure role-based access control for its data plane, because the deployment grants Key Vault Secrets Officer on it, and the deployment does not change its other settings. Find it: Azure portal > Key vaults > the vault > Properties > Resource ID. Example: kv-secops.

elements.name: existingKeyVaultResourceIdBlock

elements.toolTip: Select the Key Vault in the list above, or choose Enter the resource ID instead.

elements.name: existingKeyVaultResourceIdManual

elements.toolTip: The full resource ID of the vault that will hold the client secret. Used only with an existing vault. The provisioning identity gets Key Vault Secrets Officer on it, to store the secret. Find it: Azure portal > Key vaults > the vault > Properties > Resource ID. Example: /subscriptions/00000000-0000-0000-0000-000000000000/resourceGroups/rg-secops/providers/Microsoft.KeyVault/vaults/kv-secops. Default: this resource group.

elements.name: secretReaderObjectIdMode
elements.label: How to choose who may read the secret
elements.toolTip: Nobody for now grants no one, and you grant Key Vault Secrets User later. Enter the Object ID is for a user or a group, the usual choice: no documented form control lists users or groups, so type the ID. Pick an app is for an app registration (service principal) that reads the secret, such as an automation account. Find it: Microsoft Entra ID > Users or Groups > the user or group > Overview > Object ID, or in Cloud Shell: az ad signed-in-user show --query id -o tsv. Default: Nobody for now.

elements.name: secretReaderObjectIdManual
elements.label: Object ID of the user or group
elements.toolTip: The Object ID of a user or group that gets Key Vault Secrets User on the vault, so they can read the client secret and paste it into Abstract. Empty grants no one. Used only when a Key Vault holds the secret. Find it: Microsoft Entra ID > Users or Groups > the user or group > Overview > Object ID. Example: 11111111-1111-1111-1111-111111111111.

elements.name: secretName
elements.label: Secret name
elements.toolTip: The name of the Key Vault secret that holds the client secret. Used only when a Key Vault holds it. A redeploy reads this name to decide whether a valid secret already exists. Find it: Azure portal > Key vaults > the vault > Objects > Secrets. Example: abstract-sentinel-client-secret. Default: abstract-sentinel-client-secret.

validations.message: 1 to 127 letters, digits and hyphens.

elements.name: secretValidityYears
elements.label: Client secret validity
elements.toolTip: How many years the client secret the script creates stays valid, when a Key Vault holds it. A re-run of this template creates a new secret once the existing one expires within 30 days; enter the new value in Abstract. Find it: Microsoft Entra ID > App registrations > the app > Certificates & secrets. Example: 1. Default: 1.

elements.name: forceSecretRotation
elements.label: Create a new client secret now
elements.toolTip: Leave it off. The script creates a secret only when none exists or the existing one expires within 30 days, so a re-run is safe. On creates a new secret on this run: Abstract keeps using the old one until you enter the new value in Abstract. Find it: Microsoft Entra ID > App registrations > the app > Certificates & secrets. Default: off.

elements.name: appDisplayName
elements.label: App registration name
elements.toolTip: The display name of the Entra app the script creates for Abstract. A redeploy reuses an app only when it is the only one with this name and carries the abstract:sentinel-destination tag; otherwise the script stops. Keep the default unless your naming standard needs another name. Find it: Microsoft Entra ID > App registrations. Example: Abstract-Sentinel-App. Default: Abstract-Sentinel-App.

validations.message: 1 to 120 characters.

elements.name: azCliVersion
elements.label: Azure CLI version of the script
elements.toolTip: The Azure CLI image the deployment script runs in. Check the version is available before changing it, or the script cannot start. Example: 2.60.0. Default: 2.60.0.

validations.message: A version such as 2.60.0.
